name: Aivolut Flow – AI SEO Blog Publishing
author: Aivolut

sections.description:
Flow by Aivolut connects your WordPress site to a Flow account so you can publish posts from Flow into WordPress without creating a WordPress Application Password.

The plugin adds a WordPress settings page where an administrator can:

  • Generate or regenerate a Flow API key.
  • Copy the API key into Flow.
  • Choose the default WordPress post author used for posts published by Flow.

This plugin does not send data to Aivolut on its own. Flow calls your WordPress REST API after you paste the generated API key into Flow.

Flow is an external service operated by Aivolut. A Flow account is required to use this plugin. When you publish from Flow, Flow sends the post title, post content, excerpt, slug, taxonomy selections, post status, optional SEO metadata, and optional featured image URL to this WordPress site. If a featured image URL is provided, this WordPress site downloads that image from the provided URL and stores it in the media library.

Service terms: https://aivolut.com/terms
Privacy policy: https://aivolut.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/aivolut-flow-ai-seo-blog-publishing, or install it from the WordPress plugin directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings > Flow by Aivolut.
  4. Choose the default post author.
  5. Generate an API key and copy it into your Flow project Publishing settings.
sections.faq:
What happens when I regenerate the API key?

The old key stops working immediately. Paste the new key into Flow to reconnect the site.

Can I still use WordPress Application Passwords?

Yes. Flow supports both the plugin key method and the existing Application Password method.

Does this plugin support SEO plugin meta fields?

Yes. When exactly one supported SEO plugin is active, Flow can populate its SEO title and meta description fields for newly created posts and explicitly update selected SEO fields on existing posts. Supported plugins are Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress, and The SEO Framework. The WordPress excerpt is a separate field.

Can I update an existing WordPress post from Flow?

Yes. With version 0.3.0 or later, open the linked article in Flow and choose Update WordPress post. Select which fields to replace and confirm. Selected fields replace their WordPress values, including changes made directly in WordPress. Unselected fields, the post URL, publication settings, and comments are preserved. Saving in Flow alone does not update WordPress.

If Flow asks you to upgrade, open Plugins in WordPress and update Aivolut Flow, then retry the access check in Flow. Earlier plugin versions continue to support publishing new posts.

Does this plugin send data to Aivolut automatically?

No. The plugin waits for authenticated REST API calls from Flow. It does not send site data to Aivolut by itself.

What external services does this plugin use?

The plugin is designed to be used with Flow, an external Aivolut service. Flow calls this site’s REST API after you enter the plugin API key in Flow. When Flow sends a featured image URL, WordPress downloads that image from the URL provided by Flow.
sections.changelog:
0.3.0

  • Update selected fields of an existing WordPress post from Flow without creating another post.
  • Preserve unselected WordPress edits, URLs, publication settings, and comments.
  • Update or clear selected SEO fields with a supported SEO plugin.

0.2.0

  • Added SEO title and meta description support for Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress, and The SEO Framework.
  • Kept WordPress excerpts independent from optional SEO metadata handling.

0.1.0

  • Initial plugin API key connection.
  • Default WordPress post author setting.
  • REST endpoints for connection status, categories, taxonomy resolution, media import, post import, and post publishing.
